{"type":"ReadFile","FileContent":{"content":"1→# Work source

A work source supplies the work of orchestration runs and records their outcome. orch opens the extension point
`orch:work-source` (`unit.json` `provides.extension_points`); a command plugin of `aicore.ext.plugins` serves it.
The configuration key `work_source` of `[orch]` names the plugin (default `planner-orch`, the bridge between the
planner and orch); the plugin itself is registered by the machine in `[aicore.plugins.<id>]`. orch never names the
source or reads its files: it speaks the contract below.

## Contract `work-source/v1`
10→
`schemas/work-source/v1/input.schema.json` (`urn:swissknifeman:orch:work-source:input:v1`) and
`output.schema.json` (`…:output:v1`), contract `urn:swissknifeman:orch:work-source`, alpha. Both are closed and
choose a branch by `op`.

| Op | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claim` | `plan`, `plans_root?`, `items?` (candidate refs in order), `run_id`, `submission_id`, `actor` (`provider`, `model`, `effort?`) | `status` `claimed` \| `none` \| `blocked`; `ref`, `title`, `scenario`, `scenario_source`, `route`, `attempt_id`, `session` when claimed; `reason_code`, `message` when blocked |
| `brief` | `plan`, `plans_root?`, `ref`, `unit?`, `run_id` | `input_ref` (`artifact-ref/v1`), `input_id`, `digest`, `reused`, `artifact_id` |
| `register` | `plan`, `plans_root?`, `ref`, `run_id`, `attempt_id`, `status` (`done` \| `done_with_deviations` \| `blocked`), `report`, `evidence` (`{"V<n>": path}`), `registrar`, `executed_by` | `outcome` `recorded` \| `no-op` \| `refused`; `gate` (`verdict` `pass` \| `missing` \| `red` \| `stale` \| `none`, `checks` `{"V<n>": exit or null}`); `receipt?`; `reason_code`, `message` when refused |
20→
A refusal of the source is an answer with a `reason_code`. A plugin that fails, answers an error or answers
outside the contract is a failure of the source.

## Client

`orch.worksource.PluginWorkSource(plugin_id, *, project=None, env=None, config_file=None)` implements the
`WorkSource` protocol (`claim(**fields)`, `brief(**fields)`, `register(**fields)`, each returning the output
document). Every call looks the registration up again, validates the request (`INPUT_INVALID`, nothing is sent),
describes and invokes the plugin through `aicore.ext.plugins.invoke_one`, and validates the answer.
30→
| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `WORK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` | no registration of the plugin, a disabled or unusable one, or a plugin without the point |
| `WORK_SOURCE_FAILED` | the plugin failed, answered an error, or answered outside `work-source/v1` |
| `INPUT_INVALID` | orch built a request outside `work-source/v1` |

## The cycle: `orch.py source`

Between `source prepare` and `source register` a session or a person does the work; orch does not run stages in
40→this version. `--config FILE` applies to every command.

```text
orch.py source claim --plan P [--plans-root DIR] [--item REF]… --actor P/M[/E] [--submission-id SUB]
orch.py source brief --run RUN
orch.py source prepare --run RUN --provider P [--binding B] [--model-catalog FILE]
orch.py source register --run RUN --report FILE --status S [--evidence V#=PATH]… --actor P/M[/E] [--executed-by P/M[/E]]
```

- `claim` derives `submission_id` = `sub-` + the first 24 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON
50→  `{plan, items, actor}` (unless given) and `run_id` = `run-` + the first 24 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the
  submission, so the same arguments give the same run. A claimed run writes `run.json` (`run_id`, `submission_id`,
  `plugin`, `plan`, `plans_root`, `ref`, `attempt_id`, `scenario`, `session`) in the run directory and emits
  `orch.run.started` once per attempt; a blocked claim emits `orch.run.refused` (step `claim`). The answer is printed
  with `run_id` and `submission_id`.
- `brief` stores the brief through the source and records `input_ref` and `input_id` in `run.json`.
- `prepare` reads the brief from the artifact store of the project, loads the run-policy pack of the run's scenario
  (`orch.py policy show`), prepares a dry run with `out = <run>/prepare` and the run's `submission_id`, and writes
  `launch-plan.json`. A refusal emits `orch.run.refused` (step `prepare`).
- `register` sends the report and the evidence, writes `receipts/register.json`, and emits
60→  `orch.run.stage.finished` (stage `primary`) and `orch.run.finished` when something was recorded, or
  `orch.run.refused` (step `register`). A repeat that the source records as `no-op` emits nothing.

The run directory is `<project>/.swissknifeman/state/orch/runs/<run_id>/` inside a project (a git repository or a
folder with `.swissknifeman`), else under the machine state. Exit codes: 0 ok (`claimed`, `none`, `recorded`,
`no-op`), 1 refusal (`blocked`, `refused`, `RUN_UNKNOWN`, `RUN_NOT_BRIEFED`, `BRIEF_UNAVAILABLE`, a prepare
refusal), 2 usage, 3 `WORK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`.

## Ownership and integrity

70→- One owner per attempt: the claim starts the work under the session `run_id`; work held by another session is
  `blocked` (`ITEM_OWNED` for the planner); the port never takes work over.
- Fencing: `register` is refused (`REGISTER_STALE_OWNER`, gate `stale`) when the work is no longer held by the
  run, for example after another session took it over; nothing is written.
- Evidence gate: `done` and `done_with_deviations` need a check-evidence file with exit 0 for every acceptance
  check (`REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING`, `REGISTER_EVIDENCE_RED`); a claim in the report without a file is not a
  result. `blocked` needs none.
- Idempotency: a repeated claim of the same run returns the same attempt; a repeated register of the same attempt
  is `no-op`; a repeated brief with unchanged inputs reuses the stored brief.

# e2e-work-source.sh — end-to-end check of the work-source port of orch served by the planner-orch bridge plugin:
# orch.py source claim (and its repeat), brief (a content-addressed artifact), prepare (a valid launch-plan) and
# register through the evidence gate close a plan item; the project journal holds orch.run.started and
# orch.run.finished; a registration without evidence is refused with REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING, and a run whose item
# was taken over by another session is refused with REGISTER_STALE_OWNER.
#
# It registers the plugin in the machine configuration, so it must run in a throwaway HOME:
# scripts/dev-sandbox.sh run DIR -- bash scripts/e2e-work-source.sh. It writes only inside that HOME and a
10→# temporary folder. Exit 0 and the line "e2e work source: OK" when everything held; otherwise
# "e2e work source: FAIL ..." and exit 1.
set -euo pipefail

HUB="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/.." && pwd)"
say() { echo "e2e work source: $*" >&2; }
fail() { say "FAIL $*"; exit 1; }

real_home="$(python3 -c 'import os, pwd; print(pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir)' 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$real_home" ] || [ "$(readlink -f "${HOME:-/}")" = "$(readlink -f "$real_home")" ]; then
20→  echo "SKM_DEV_GUARD: e2e-work-source.sh changes the machine configuration; run it with a throwaway HOME (scripts/dev-sandbox.sh)" >&2
  exit 3
fi

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
# The partners of the bridge, as scripts/test-bridges.sh wires them from the hub layout.
export PLANNER_ROOT="$HUB/packages/planner"
export PLANNER_PLAN_PY="$PLANNER_ROOT/scripts/plan.py"
export SKM_ORCH_ROOT="$HUB/packages/orch"
30→export AICORE_ROOT="$HUB/packages/aicore"
export SKM_AICORE_EVENTS__DELIVERY=off
export PYTHONPATH="$SKM_ORCH_ROOT/lib:$AICORE_ROOT/lib${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
aicore() { python3 -m aicore "$@"; }
plan() { python3 "$PLANNER_PLAN_PY" "$@"; }
orch() { python3 "$SKM_ORCH_ROOT/scripts/orch.py" "$@"; }
field() { python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))[sys.argv[2]])' "$@"; }

aicore config set aicore.plugins.planner-orch.manifest "$HUB/bridges/planner-orch/extension.json" --machine >/dev/null
aicore config set aicore.plugins.planner-orch.trusted true --machine >/dev/null

PROJECT="$WORK/project"

git init -q "$PROJECT"
cd "$PROJECT"
ACTOR="claude-code/claude-opus-5-5/high"
plan new --plans-root plans --codename WS --title "Work source" --repository e2e --owner e2e --actor "$ACTOR" \

50→[ -n "$PLAN_ID" ] || fail "no plan was created"

plan set "$PLAN_ID" P1 --json '{"goal": "g"}' >/dev/null || fail "set phase"
for n in 1 2 3; do

    "validation": [{"id": "V1", "cmd": "true", "expect": "exit 0", "kind": "acceptance"}]}' >/dev/null || fail "add-item $n"

60→  {"id": "B2", "items": ["P1.2"], "mode": "recommended"}, {"id": "B3", "items": ["P1.3"], "mode": "recommended"}]' \
  >/dev/null || fail "batches"

evidence() {  # evidence <item> <exit>: a check-evidence file of V1, repository-relative path on stdout
  mkdir -p ev

[ "$(field "$WORK/claim.json" status)" = claimed ] || fail "claim: $(cat "$WORK/claim.json")"
[ "$(field "$WORK/claim.json" ref)" = P1.1 ] || fail "claim took $(field "$WORK/claim.json" ref), expected P1.1"
RUN="$(field "$WORK/claim.json" run_id)"
ATTEMPT="$(field "$WORK/claim.json" attempt_id)"
orch source claim --plan "$PLAN_ID" --actor "$ACTOR" > "$WORK/claim-again.json" || fail "repeated claim"
[ "$(field "$WORK/claim-again.json" attempt_id)" = "$ATTEMPT" ] || fail "the repeated claim changed the attempt"
80→[ "$(field "$WORK/claim-again.json" run_id)" = "$RUN" ] || fail "the repeated claim changed the run"
say "ok: claimed P1.1 as $RUN; a repeat is the same run and attempt"

orch source brief --run "$RUN" > "$WORK/brief.json" || fail "source brief"
python3 - "$WORK/brief.json" "$PROJECT" <<'EOF' || fail "the brief blob is missing"
import json, sys
from aicore.state import blobs
answer = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
assert blobs.blob_path(answer["input_ref"], project=sys.argv[2]).is_file(), answer
EOF
90→say "ok: the brief is stored as $(field "$WORK/brief.json" artifact_id)"

orch source prepare --run "$RUN" --provider claude-code --binding claude-only > /dev/null || fail "source prepare"
RUN_DIR="$PROJECT/.swissknifeman/state/orch/runs/$RUN"
orch validate launch-plan "$RUN_DIR/launch-plan.json" --quiet || fail "launch-plan.json is not valid"
say "ok: launch-plan.json is valid"

orch source register --run "$RUN" --report "$WORK/report.json" --status done --evidence "V1=$(evidence P1.1 0)" \
  --actor "$ACTOR" > "$WORK/register.json" || fail "source register: $(cat "$WORK/register.json")"
[ "$(field "$WORK/register.json" outcome)" = recorded ] || fail "register: $(cat "$WORK/register.json")"
100→[ "$(status_of P1.1)" = done ] || fail "P1.1 is $(status_of P1.1), expected done"
[ -f "$RUN_DIR/receipts/register.json" ] || fail "no registration receipt in the run"
types="$(aicore events list --project "$PROJECT" --type 'orch.*' --json | python3 -c '
import json, sys
print(" ".join(e["type"] for e in json.load(sys.stdin)["events"]))')"
case " $types " in *" orch.run.started "*" orch.run.finished "*) ;; *) fail "journal types: $types" ;; esac
say "ok: P1.1 is done; the journal holds $types"

# 2. A registration without evidence is refused and writes nothing.
orch source claim --plan "$PLAN_ID" --item P1.2 --actor "$ACTOR" > "$WORK/claim2.json" || fail "claim P1.2"
110→RUN2="$(field "$WORK/claim2.json" run_id)"
set +e
orch source register --run "$RUN2" --report "$WORK/report.json" --status done --actor "$ACTOR" > "$WORK/register2.json"
code=$?
set -e
[ "$code" = 1 ] || fail "register without evidence exited $code, expected 1"
[ "$(field "$WORK/register2.json" reason_code)" = REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING ] || fail "register2: $(cat "$WORK/register2.json")"
[ "$(status_of P1.2)" = in_progress ] || fail "P1.2 changed to $(status_of P1.2)"
say "ok: a registration without evidence is refused with REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING"

120→# 3. Another session takes the item over: the old run registers nothing.
orch source claim --plan "$PLAN_ID" --item P1.3 --actor "$ACTOR" > "$WORK/claim3.json" || fail "claim P1.3"
RUN3="$(field "$WORK/claim3.json" run_id)"
plan start "$PLAN_ID" P1.3 --actor "$ACTOR" --session other-session --take-over --no-scout >/dev/null || fail "take-over"
set +e
orch source register --run "$RUN3" --report "$WORK/report.json" --status done --evidence "V1=$(evidence P1.3 0)" \
  --actor "$ACTOR" > "$WORK/register3.json"
code=$?
set -e
[ "$code" = 1 ] || fail "register after the take-over exited $code, expected 1"
130→[ "$(field "$WORK/register3.json" reason_code)" = REGISTER_STALE_OWNER ] || fail "register3: $(cat "$WORK/register3.json")"
[ "$(status_of P1.3)" = in_progress ] || fail "P1.3 changed to $(status_of P1.3)"
say "ok: the run that lost its item is refused with REGISTER_STALE_OWNER"

echo "e2e work source: OK"

class SourceRefusal(Exception):
270→    """A refusal of a ``source`` command: ``CODE: message`` on stderr and ``exit`` (1, or 3 without a source)."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, exit_code: int = 1):

280→    """``PROVIDER/MODEL[/EFFORT]`` as a work-source actor."""

    if len(parts) not in (2, 3) or not all(parts):

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the cycle of a work source

RUN_DOC = "run.json"
LAUNCH_PLAN_DOC = "launch-plan.json"
REGISTER_RECEIPT = "receipts/register.json"
STAGE_STATUS = {"done": "completed", "done_with_deviations": "completed", "blocked": "failed"}


class SourceRefusal(Exception):
    """A refusal of a ``source`` command: ``CODE: message`` on stderr and ``exit`` (1, or 3 without a source)."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, exit_code: int = 1):
        super().__init__(f"{code}: {message}")
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.exit_code = exit_code


def _actor(text: str) -> dict:
    """``PROVIDER/MODEL[/EFFORT]`` as a work-source actor."""
    parts = text.split("/") if isinstance(text, str) else []
    if len(parts) not in (2, 3) or not all(parts):
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{text!r} must be PROVIDER/MODEL[/EFFORT]")
    return dict(zip(("provider", "model", "effort"), parts))


def _evidence(text: str) -> tuple:
    check_id, sep, path = text.partition("=")
    if not sep or not path or not check_id[:1] == "V" or not check_id[1:].isdigit():
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{text!r} must be V<n>=PATH")
    return check_id, path


def submission_id(plan: str, items: list, actor: dict) -> str:
    """The default submission of a claim: the same plan, items and actor give the same submission (and run)."""
    return "sub-" + sha256_hex(canonical_json_bytes({"plan": plan, "items": list(items), "actor": actor}))[:24]


def run_id_of(submission: str) -> str:
    return "run-" + sha256_hex(submission.encode("utf-8"))[:24]


def _source(current: settings.Settings, project, config_file) -> PluginWorkSource:
    return PluginWorkSource(current.work_source, project=project, config_file=config_file)


def _call(source: PluginWorkSource, op: str, **fields) -> dict:
    try:
        return getattr(source, op)(**fields)
    except WorkSourceError as error:
        raise SourceRefusal(error.code, error.message, 3 if error.code == "WORK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE" else 1) from None


def _run(run_id: str, project) -> tuple:
    """``(run directory, run.json)`` of a claimed run; ``RUN_UNKNOWN`` when it was never claimed here."""
    directory = journal.run_dir(run_id, project=project)
    doc = journal.read_doc(directory, RUN_DOC)
    if doc is None:
        raise SourceRefusal("RUN_UNKNOWN", f"no claimed run {run_id} in {directory.parent}")
    return directory, doc


def _emit(event_type: str, data: dict, *, subject: str, current, project, config_file) -> None:
    events.emit(event_type, {key: value for key, value in data.items() if value is not None}, subject=subject,
                settings=current, project=project, config_file=config_file)


def _print(doc: dict) -> None:
    print(json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))


def _source_claim(args, current, project) -> int:
    actor, items = args.actor, list(args.item or [])
    submission = args.submission_id or submission_id(args.plan, items, actor)
    run_id = run_id_of(submission)
    directory = journal.run_dir(run_id, project=project)
    before = journal.read_doc(directory, RUN_DOC)
    emit = dict(current=current, project=project, config_file=args.config)
    # A repeated claim asks for the run's own item, so a run never moves on to other work once its item is closed.
    asked = [before["ref"]] if before is not None and before.get("ref") else items
    try:
        answer = _call(_source(current, project, args.config), "claim", plan=args.plan, plans_root=args.plans_root,
                       items=asked or None, run_id=run_id, submission_id=submission, actor=actor)
    except SourceRefusal as refusal:
        _emit("orch.run.refused", {"submission_id": submission, "step": "claim", "reason_codes": [refusal.code],
                                   "run_id": run_id}, subject=submission, **emit)
        raise
    _print({"run_id": run_id, "submission_id": submission, **answer})
    if answer["status"] == "claimed":
        doc = {"run_id": run_id, "submission_id": submission, "plugin": current.work_source, "plan": args.plan,
               "plans_root": args.plans_root, "ref": answer["ref"], "attempt_id": answer["attempt_id"],
               "scenario": answer.get("scenario"), "session": answer.get("session")}
        if before is not None:  # a repeated claim keeps what later steps recorded (input_ref)
            doc = {**before, **doc}
        journal.write_doc(directory, RUN_DOC, doc)
        if before is None or before.get("attempt_id") != doc["attempt_id"]:
            _emit("orch.run.started", {"run_id": run_id, "submission_id": submission, "attempt_id": doc["attempt_id"],
                                       "source": {"plugin": current.work_source, "ref": doc["ref"]},
                                       "scenario": doc["scenario"]}, subject=run_id, **emit)
        return 0
    if answer["status"] == "blocked":
        _emit("orch.run.refused", {"submission_id": submission, "step": "claim", "run_id": run_id,
                                   "reason_codes": [answer.get("reason_code") or "CLAIM_BLOCKED"],
                                   "ref": answer.get("ref")}, subject=submission, **emit)
        return 1
    return 0


def _source_brief(args, current, project) -> int:
    directory, doc = _run(args.run, project)
    answer = _call(_source(current, project, args.config), "brief", plan=doc["plan"], plans_root=doc.get("plans_root"),
                   ref=doc["ref"], run_id=doc["run_id"])
    journal.write_doc(directory, RUN_DOC, {**doc, "input_ref": answer["input_ref"], "input_id": answer["input_id"]})
    _print(answer)
    return 0


def _brief_doc(doc: dict, project) -> dict:
    from aicore.state import blobs
    if not isinstance(doc.get("input_ref"), dict):
        raise SourceRefusal("RUN_NOT_BRIEFED", f"run {doc['run_id']} has no brief; run source brief first")
    try:
        found = json.loads(blobs.read_bytes(doc["input_ref"], project=project))
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise SourceRefusal("BRIEF_UNAVAILABLE", f"the brief {doc['input_ref']['digest']} is not in the artifact "
                            "store of this project") from None
    except ValueError as error:
        raise SourceRefusal("BRIEF_UNAVAILABLE", str(error)) from None
    if not isinstance(found, dict):
        raise SourceRefusal("BRIEF_UNAVAILABLE", "the stored brief is not a JSON object")
    return found


def _source_prepare(args, current, project) -> int:
    directory, doc = _run(args.run, project)
    emit = dict(current=current, project=project, config_file=args.config)
    refused = {"submission_id": doc["submission_id"], "step": "prepare", "run_id": doc["run_id"], "ref": doc["ref"],
               "policy_id": doc.get("scenario"), "binding": args.binding}
    try:
        input_doc = _brief_doc(doc, project)
        policy = policies.load(doc.get("scenario") or current.default_profile, current)
        plan = _dry_run(input_doc, policy, current, out=directory / "prepare", provider=args.provider,
                        binding_flag=args.binding, model_catalog=args.model_catalog,
                        submission_id=doc["submission_id"])
    except PortError as error:
        report = error.data.get("launch_plan")
        codes = [error.code] + [item["reason_code"] for item in (report or {}).get("refusals", [])
                                if item.get("reason_code") and item["reason_code"] != error.code]
        _emit("orch.run.refused", {**refused, "reason_codes": codes}, subject=doc["submission_id"], **emit)
        print(f"{error.code}: {error.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        if report:
            _print(report)
        return 1
    except (SourceRefusal, policies.PolicyError, catalog.CatalogError, launch.LaunchError,
            settings.SettingsError) as error:
        _emit("orch.run.refused", {**refused, "reason_codes": [error.code]}, subject=doc["submission_id"], **emit)
        raise SourceRefusal(error.code, error.message if isinstance(error, SourceRefusal) else str(error)) from None
    journal.write_doc(directory, LAUNCH_PLAN_DOC, plan)
    _print(plan)
    return 0


def _source_register(args, current, project) -> int:
    directory, doc = _run(args.run, project)
    try:
        report = json.loads(Path(args.report).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        raise SourceRefusal("INPUT_INVALID", f"cannot read the report {args.report}: {error}") from None
    evidence = dict(args.evidence or [])
    if len(evidence) != len(args.evidence or []):
        raise SourceRefusal("INPUT_INVALID", "--evidence repeats a check id")
    answer = _call(_source(current, project, args.config), "register", plan=doc["plan"],
                   plans_root=doc.get("plans_root"), ref=doc["ref"], run_id=doc["run_id"],
                   attempt_id=doc["attempt_id"], status=args.status, report=report, evidence=evidence,
                   registrar=args.actor, executed_by=args.executed_by or args.actor)
    journal.write_doc(directory, REGISTER_RECEIPT, answer)
    _print(answer)
    emit = dict(current=current, project=project, config_file=args.config)
    if answer["outcome"] == "refused":
        _emit("orch.run.refused", {"submission_id": doc["submission_id"], "step": "register", "run_id": doc["run_id"],
                                   "ref": doc["ref"], "reason_codes": [answer.get("reason_code") or "REGISTER_REFUSED"]},
              subject=doc["submission_id"], **emit)
        return 1
    if answer["outcome"] == "recorded":  # a repeat that changed nothing (no-op) is not a second end of the run
        _emit("orch.run.stage.finished", {"run_id": doc["run_id"], "stage_id": "primary", "attempt": 1,
                                          "status": STAGE_STATUS[args.status], "attempt_id": doc["attempt_id"]},
              subject=doc["run_id"], **emit)
        _emit("orch.run.finished", {"run_id": doc["run_id"], "submission_id": doc["submission_id"], "ref": doc["ref"],
                                    "attempt_id": doc["attempt_id"], "outcome": args.status,
                                    "gate": answer["gate"]["verdict"]}, subject=doc["run_id"], **emit)
    return 0


def _source_command(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    handler = {"claim": _source_claim, "brief": _source_brief, "prepare": _source_prepare,
               "register": _source_register}[args.action]
    try:
        project = _project_root()
        current = settings.load(project=project, config_file=args.config)  # the configuration is read once
        return handler(args, current, project)
    except SourceRefusal as refusal:
        print(f"{refusal.code}: {refusal.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return refusal.exit_code
    except PortError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except ConfigError as error:
        print(f"CONFIG_INVALID: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except settings.SettingsError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

def run(cwd, *argv, check=True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(PLAN_PY), *argv], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          encoding="utf-8", check=False)

class Template:
    """One temporary plan with three items in three batches, built once and copied for every test."""

    root: Path | None = None

    @classmethod
    def build(cls) -> Path:
        if cls.root is None:
            cls.root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ws-template-"))
            project = cls.root / "project"
            (project / "plans").mkdir(parents=True)
            subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", str(project)], check=True)
            run(project, "new", "--plans-root", "plans", "--codename", "WS", "--title", "Work source",
                "--repository", "ws", "--owner", "ws", "--actor", ACTOR_TEXT, "--message", "m", "--date", "2026.10.07")
            plan = next((project / "plans").iterdir()).name
            run(project, "add-phase", plan, "--title", "One")
            run(project, "set", plan, "P1", "--json", json.dumps({"goal": "g"}))
            for index, title in enumerate(("A", "B", "C"), 1):
                item = dict(ITEM, task_files=[{"path": f"lib/{title}.py", "change": "any"}])
                run(project, "add-item", plan, "P1", "--title", title, "--json", json.dumps(item))
            run(project, "batches", plan, "P1", "--json", json.dumps(
                [{"id": f"B{n}", "items": [f"P1.{n}"], "mode": "recommended"} for n in (1, 2, 3)]))
            run(project, "set", plan, "P1.3", "--json", json.dumps({"orchestration": {"scenario": "nope"}}))
            run(project, "design-done", plan, "P1", "--actor", ACTOR_TEXT)
        return cls.root / "project"

    @classmethod
    def cleanup(cls) -> None:
        if cls.root is not None:
            shutil.rmtree(cls.root, ignore_errors=True)
            cls.root = None

Finally, they ruled out a double-reply bug: when `invoke` replies and returns early for a brief operation, `main` does not reply again.

The reviewer will run the describe test to verify digest_json matches aicore expectations. They are also inspecting planner finish for evidence gate behavior and preparing to run tests in parallel with critical planner and aicore functions. A suspicious code snippet in worksource op_brief was noted.

The reviewer is inspecting the blob reuse logic in `op_brief`. This mismatch could cause the blob path check to fail even when the artifact reference is valid.

The reviewer confirmed that `doc["digest"]` is the hash of the payload, while the blob address is the hash of the full document including the digest field. This mismatch is acceptable if the schema's input_ref is an artifact reference with its own digest. They also noted that `put_json` might hash the stored content differently than `canonical_json_bytes(doc)`, which would break blob reuse.

The reviewer is now checking whether `put_json` hashes the stored bytes identically to `canonical_json_bytes(doc)`. If the two differ, blob reuse would fail and a new blob might be written each time. The test expects `reused` to stay true on a second call with identical input, so the first write must have stored exactly those canonical bytes.

The reviewer will run the tests to verify that `again["reused"]` is True, which confirms the blob reuse logic works. They are also inspecting the evidence gate for a bug where a check file has exit code 0 but the gate compares the wrong check. They confirmed that validation checks live under the `validation` key, and missing evidence takes precedence over red evidence.

The evidence gate returns MISSING when a check file lacks the required `exit` field, even if it contains `"result": 0`. This is acceptable because the contract only requires `exit` or a pass verdict. The reviewer will inspect the planner check-evidence schema to ensure no valid pass shape is missed.

The evidence gate checks that a check_id matches but does not verify the subject. A file for one item could be reused for another if the IDs collide, though the contract does not require subject binding. This is a skipped edge case. Duplicate check IDs in the acceptance list are unlikely.

The reviewer is checking whether evidence paths resolve relative to the plans repository rather than the current working directory. They also spotted a likely logic bug in `op_register`: the outcome is marked "recorded" if any call was recorded, even when a later attempt partially failed and never finished.

The reviewer confirmed that `op_register` correctly handles retries and repeats. They also spotted a fragile bug: the handler detects no-op outcomes by checking the first line of `plan.py` stdout for the substring " already registered (attempt ". If `plan.py` prints a JSON line first, this check will fail.

The reviewer suspects a concrete no-op detection bug in `op_register`. The handler searches for the substring `" already registered (attempt "` at the start of `plan.py` stdout. If the planner prints the no-op message without that leading space, the check fails and the repeat is wrongly marked as "recorded". This would violate idempotency and emit a duplicate `orch.run.finished` event.

The reviewer confirmed that log idempotency is handled by the bridge's journal check rather than the message content. A journal read failure returns an error after the guard but before any writes, so it is safe. If no log calls exist, the finish step runs directly without reading the journal. They also noted that the final `next` command is a read and does not trigger the fence.

The reviewer spotted a crash risk in `check_owner`: if the executor field is a string rather than an object, `.get("session")` raises an `AttributeError`. This would crash `register.py` with exit code 1.

The `check_owner` crash would produce exit code 1. The worksource treats this as a normal refusal, so the outcome becomes REGISTER_REFUSED and nothing is written. This only matters if the executor field is ever a string instead of an object.

The reviewer confirmed that `read_item` safely returns `None` when JSON parsing fails, producing a conservative `REGISTER_ITEM_UNREADABLE` outcome. They also noted that `plan.py --output json` might emit logs before the JSON payload, which would break parsing. Next they will inspect the CLI submission hash and actor key ordering.

The reviewer suspects the default plugin ID `planner-orch` in the orchestrator settings violates contract 9, which forbids the core from naming partner packages. They will read the boundary tests to confirm whether this is a real violation.
I am examining the start and finish functions for ownership and attempt_id. I will also review the attempt_id pattern.

A critical finding area has been identified.

The `_owner_conflict` logic correctly blocks items when the session or provider differs. The finish step intentionally skips ownership checks; the fence is enforced in register.py before plan.py is called.

A repeat-after-lost-answer bug was found. The finish step stores `attempt_id` in the result. Afterward, the executor is replaced with `executed_by`, which lacks the session. The owner check then matches on `attempt_id` alone and allows a repeat.

The repeat-after-lost-answer concern was unfounded. On a repeat, register.py passes evidence but not checks, so finish rebuilds checks from evidence and finds them matching the recorded attempt. The owner check therefore does not allow a repeat.

The no-op detection in register.py searches for `" already registered (attempt "` with a leading space. The finish output prints the same phrase without that space, so the check fails to recognize the no-op.

The no-op detection is actually correct. The item ID precedes the finish output, so the search string matches without needing a leading space.

I still need to verify that the attempt ID format matches the planner's ATTEMPT_ID regex, or finish will raise ATTEMPT_ID_INVALID.

The evidence gate still runs on repeats of closed items. It passes because the retry includes the required evidence files. If the report has no open issues, finish is a no-op and the outcome is no-op. If there are open issues, existing logs are skipped and finish remains a no-op. The outcome stays no-op in both cases.

A sequencing bug was found in finish. Evidence validation runs before the attempt_id idempotency check. If evidence files are missing on retry, finish raises EVIDENCE_INVALID instead of returning already_registered.

The evidence gate in register.py also runs before the write and would refuse with REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING. The sequencing concern is resolved: a missing evidence file on retry raises before _commit, so no write occurs. The attempt ID regex still needs to be checked.

A new owner-fencing bug was found. If an item is reopened after a prior finish, the old `attempt_id` may be preserved. A new session then claiming the item would pass `check_owner` because the attempt ID matches, even though a different session now owns it.

Take-over replaces the executor and its session, so an old attempt_id cannot block a new owner. The remaining risk is reopen: if a finished item is reopened and then taken by another session, the preserved attempt_id might still allow the wrong owner to register.

The scenario check in `op_claim` runs before the route check in `start`. This ordering could allow a claim to pass scenario validation while the route check still fails.

The scenario check in `op_claim` runs before `start`, so a failed scenario blocks the claim before any write. The context collection and build inside `start` occur after the lock and are intended writes. I am now checking whether `plan.py` context writes files.

The `orchestration` variable is built from `plan.py context --stdout` before the scenario guard. If that command writes files, it would be a plan write occurring before the claim is blocked by an unknown scenario.

The `brief.build` step may also write context packs. The evidence gate's `evidence_exit` check is weaker than the planner's `_load_evidence`, so the remaining checks in that function need review.

The evidence gate's weaker validation could let finish reject an item after logs are already written. The existing test for missing evidence covers this by checking that no logs are produced when the gate fails first.

The evidence gate omits the subject check that the planner enforces. A file with the correct check_id and exit code but a wrong subject passes the gate yet fails finish with EVIDENCE_INVALID. If the item has open issues, those logs are written before finish rejects.

A done report with no open issues causes finish to fail atomically. Nothing is written and the outcome is refused. The receipt records a gate pass followed by a refused finish call. The item remains open. This is acceptable when no logs exist.

The wrong-subject evidence gate concern is not a contract violation. The gate only checks exit code or verdict pass, not subject. If finish rejects the item, it does so with EVIDENCE_INVALID and no plan write occurs.

A wrong-subject evidence file that passes the gate causes a partial write. The note is logged before finish rejects, leaving a stray entry in the plan. On retry, the no-op check skips the duplicate note, but finish still fails and the item remains in_progress with an orphaned note.

The partial-write concern is not a new defect. The register.py log-then-finish pattern predates the evidence gate, and the gate only adds a pre-check rather than replacing finish validation. I am now checking whether the gate omits any contract requirements that finish must enforce.

Contract 4 is fully implemented by the evidence gate. A potential hole was found: acceptance checks may reside in phase validation rather than `doc["validation"]`, and finish includes phase validation while the gate does not.

The acceptance check concern is resolved. The gate and finish both draw acceptance checks from the item validation list, so phase-level checks are not missed.

Evidence paths are correctly shared between the gate and finish.

A new discrepancy was found: a `checks_run` claim with exit 0 becomes `--check` when the evidence gate is off, but it does not when the gate is on.

The plan calls are assembled before the guard runs, so a guard refusal prevents any execution. When the gate is on, a checks_run claim with exit 1 is ignored and only --evidence is added; finish uses the evidence exit code. If an evidence file has the wrong check_id, the gate returns MISSING.

The evidence gate rejects a directory path as missing evidence. Boolean exit codes are correctly excluded from integer checks.

A done item with no acceptance checks passes the gate and finish without evidence. The contract only requires evidence files for checks that exist.

For blocked items, the gate returns early without checking evidence files. The plan call may still include --evidence flags if evidence was passed, but --check is suppressed. Finish does not require acceptance checks for blocked items.

The evidence gate rejects red checks with exit codes other than zero. This prevents closing an item as done_with_deviations when an acceptance check is red. The contract requires evidence files for every acceptance check, but it does not explicitly forbid red checks from blocking that close type.

The evidence gate rejects red checks for both done and done_with_deviations, while the planner only blocks done. This is a contract violation.

The stricter gate for done_with_deviations is correct per the contract, so that concern is resolved. Guard ordering is confirmed safe. The attempt_id regex and CLI session parsing still need review. Repeated claims from the same session resume the item successfully.

The attempt_id is computed by the bridge, not stored by start. After finish, a repeated claim raises ITEM_NOT_STARTABLE because the item is no longer startable. The contract requires a repeated claim with the same run_id to return the same attempt. This is violated after an item is finished. It may be out of scope since idempotency applies only while holding the item.

A same-session claim for a finished item returns blocked with exit 1 and emits `orch.run.refused`, leaving the run file intact. The CLI may still retry this claim, which would be refused again.

When a session holds an in-progress item and a second todo item is started under the same run_id, the candidate function returns that new item instead of resuming the original. This yields a different reference and attempt_id, which may violate the contract requiring identical answers for repeated claims.

The same-session claim discrepancy is not a bug. The contract's "same run_id" refers to the run identifier alone, not to the item list. The CLI prevents this by forcing the original reference on repeat, and the plugin's candidate function prefers the running item owned by that run when items are omitted.

The test suite only covers same-session repeats while an item is running. It does not exercise the case where a different item list is passed, so that behavior remains untested.

A provider mismatch is treated as an owner conflict even when the session is identical. This is not a bug.

The claim path correctly omits `--take-over`. Policy is shown before start. Calling `plan.py context` when the scenario is unknown is expensive but not a defect.

A valid scenario with a slow or misconfigured `orch.py policy show` incorrectly blocks the item. This is an environment issue rather than a code defect.

`partners.require_orch()` raises `SystemExit` on failure, which is acceptable.

The attempt ID pattern and length are being compared between the work-source and planner implementations.

The finish code preserves the executor and started_at fields from the prior state, then replaces executor with executed_by. The attempt_id is stored in attribution. A retry with a slightly different evidence path string but the same file causes the gate to pass, yet finish raises ATTEMPT_CONFLICT. The outcome is refused rather than a no-op.

The CLI writes the receipt before emitting events, and a refused claim still produces a receipt. A solid bug was identified: `op_claim` calls `policy_exists`, which shells to `orch.py`; the plan scenario may be the default "solo" from orchestration.

The `context` command works for todo items and is not a defect. A new ordering bug was found: if the item route is missing class or effort, the answer includes a partial route that fails schema validation after start has already occurred.

The plugin adds the route to the answer before executing the start command. If the route is incomplete, the item starts successfully but the orchestrator client rejects the answer because of schema validation. The CLI does not write the run file in this case, yet the item remains started.

The attempt_id regex permits `@` in run IDs, but the generated attempt_id string does not. This mismatch would cause the orchestrator client to reject the answer after the item has already started.

The `@` in run_id schema mismatch is a real contract bug. A valid run_id containing `@` cannot form a valid attempt_id, so the orchestrator client rejects the answer after the item has already started. Reproduction: claim with a run_id containing `@`, then finish; the orchestrator rejects the output.

A max-length run_id plus a reference could exceed the attempt_id limit, but the CLI generates only 28-character IDs so this is not triggered in practice. The session field accepts any non-empty string, while attempt_id has stricter constraints, confirming the schema mismatch. The reviewer is now examining `problems()` for validation issues with oneOf exclusivity and external references.

The `_owner_conflict` check only compares session and provider, not model or effort. A repeated claim with a different effort value therefore passes the conflict check, but the answer is built from the item document so it remains consistent.

The `reused` flag in the brief is being examined.

This path comparison needs verification against the storage logic. The `add-artifact` command correctly targets the item when the reference includes a unit. The `_previous_brief` function properly compares units.

The brief is rebuilt on every call even when reused, and add-artifact might not be idempotent. The test suite already checks that the artifact list length stays at one after a second brief, so it appears safe. The reviewer is now examining canonical for submission_id versus contract mismatches.

The contract specifies `sha256_hex(canonical(plan, items, actor))`, but the code hashes raw bytes from `canonical_json_bytes`. This is a real defect: the hash is computed over JSON serialization rather than the canonical form. The reviewer also notes that `run_id` is derived from `submission_id` via `sha256_hex(submission.encode("utf-8"))`, which hashes the raw string instead of its canonical JSON representation.

Hashing raw UTF-8 bytes is the correct interpretation of the contract.

A new ordering bug was found in `_source_claim`: it emits `orch.run.refused` for every `SourceRefusal`, including `WORK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INPUT_INVALID`, and `WORK_SOURCE_FAILED`. The existing CLI test for missing plugins only checks exit code and stderr, so it never verifies that no event was emitted. This means the ordering bug is untested.

The reviewer will reproduce the ordering bug with a small script. A blocked status also emits an event without writing the run journal, though the documentation explicitly describes this behavior.

The blocked-claim event is not a doc disagreement because the documentation explicitly permits it. The unavailable-source event emission is the clearer defect, since the code violates the user contract item 8 that events must only be emitted after the run journal is written.

The documentation explicitly lists blocked claims, prepare refusals, and register refusals as the only cases that emit `orch.run.refused`. It does not mention `WORK_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` at all. The code emits the event for every `SourceRefusal`, including unavailable sources. This is a direct doc-code disagreement.

A reproduction script will claim a run without the plugin to confirm the event is emitted and no run journal is written.

Prepare and register refusals are handled differently. Prepare catches errors, emits an event, and raises. Register does not catch SourceRefusal from plugin failures; it propagates up to _source_command, which prints the error without emitting an event or writing a receipt. This means a failed register produces no event or receipt at all.

The reviewer now considers the missing register event acceptable because it avoids a false event, unlike the claim path. They are shifting focus to more serious behavioral bugs, specifically examining `load_evidence`, the check-evidence subject requirement, and whether the gate fails to reject red verdicts when both exit code 0 and verdict checks fail.

The evidence gate and finish command may use divergent resolvers. If the gate resolves a path to None while finish accepts it, the gate incorrectly rejects the run as MISSING. The reviewer is now reading `context._resolve` and the evidence subject check to verify this.

A resolver divergence between the evidence gate and finish is a real defect if the contract condition is met but the gate misses the file. The unit reference parsing in main() correctly splits `P1.1/U1/extra` into item and unit, and guard checks ownership on the parent item for units.

The evidence gate is skipped for unit returns even when status is done. The register command accepts unit references, so a client could submit a unit return with --gate evidence and bypass acceptance checks.

The reviewer is now checking the README and design documents to determine whether skipping evidence acceptance for unit returns is an intentional exception or a contract violation.

The evidence gate correctly omits `--check` flags for checks already present in the evidence list. If a V2 check is missing from evidence, it does not block the gate unless it is an acceptance check; otherwise finish will not receive that result.

The attempt_id format `att-run-<hex>-<ref>` is 37 characters long. The regex allows up to 128 characters, so the length is not the issue.

The work-source schema allows attempt_ids up to 204 characters. The planner only allows 128. If a run_id is 160 characters long, the resulting attempt_id reaches 169 characters. The planner would reject it with ATTEMPT_ID_INVALID.

The planner regex does not allow slashes. The work-source schema does. A reference like `P1.1/U1` would create an attempt_id containing `/`. The planner would reject it with ATTEMPT_ID_INVALID.

The bridge passes attempt_id through to register.py. A slash in the attempt id would therefore break unit registration. Item refs use dots, which are allowed, so item operations should be unaffected.

The slash and length mismatches are not triggered by the CLI formulas. The evidence gate is missing several planner checks: schema, subject format, candidate head, producer kind, and observation for procedures.

The contract only requires the gate to check exit code or verdict, so this gap is not a contract violation. If no logs are written, finish fails atomically inside the mutation and nothing is committed.

If the report contains a note, the log is written before finish. When evidence passes the weak gate but fails the planner's stricter check, this creates a real write-before-guard bug. The contract only restricts writes for gate refusals; once the gate passes, writes proceed regardless of the subsequent finish failure.

The gate passes on exit code alone, but the planner rejects the evidence during finish. Because register.py logs before finish, a partial write occurs even though the registration cannot succeed. This is a real defect: the gate should guard against writing invalid evidence, yet it does not.

The gate also accepts evidence that contains both `exit` and `verdict`, which the planner rejects. This creates another partial-write bug where finish later fails.

I am now examining the `next` command and claim candidate selection for a logic bug.

The `_candidate` function returns a running item owned by the current run_id, then falls back to the first item in a `run-items` lane, and finally to the next upcoming item or a reason string. This ordering is being checked for logic flaws.

A bug was found in the claim candidate selection logic. The `next --parallel 1` command may only return a single lane, so the current run's item could be missing from the `running` list. If another item is selected instead, repeated claims with the same run_id would yield different answers, violating the contract that repeated claims must be deterministic.

The `_candidate` function claims the first item in a `run-items` lane even when the current run already holds a different item. This allows one run to own multiple items simultaneously.

A race condition exists in the claim-and-start flow. Two parallel CLI claims with identical arguments can both see no run.json, call start with the same session, and write their own run.json. Because start is idempotent for the same session, both writes succeed and both emit an `orch.run.started` event. This produces a duplicate event.

I am checking whether the journal or event system has idempotency keys to prevent duplicate writes.

A reproduction script outside the repository could simulate the owner-fence race by importing register and mocking timing. The race is difficult to trigger reliably because no hook exists between the guard check and execution.

A concrete reproduction for the owner-fence race is now planned. An external script will import register.main and patch guard or run_plan to simulate a takeover between the ownership check and the finish call. This proves that finish proceeds after the guard check, confirming the stale-session bug.

The owner-fence race is a real defect. The fence checks ownership once before writing, but finish never re-verifies it. Another session can take over the item in that window, violating the contract that requires the item to be held by SESSION before any plan write.

The evidence gate accepts a valid file for the wrong subject. Finish later rejects it with EVIDENCE_SUBJECT. If no logs were written, the registration fails closed and produces no partial write.

The gate cannot cause a false success because finish strictly enforces the subject. The partial-write bug is deterministic and will be verified with a reproduction script.

The gate's acceptance criteria may be intentionally minimal, matching the parenthetical summary in the contract rather than the full planner schema. I am checking the bridge README and register comments to confirm whether the gate is meant to enforce the complete evidence contract.

{"type":"ReadFile","FileContent":{"content":"1→# Bridge planner ↔ orch (`planner-orch`)

The only place where the planner knows the orch execution contract `exec/v1`. The planner core stays neutral;
replacing the orchestrator means adding another bridge under `bridges/`, not editing the core. The bridge is a unit
of the hub (`unit.json`, kind `bridge`); the planner finds it through `bridges.roots` of its configuration.

| Verb | Entrypoint | Direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brief` | `brief.py` | Task → orch: plan item or unit as an `execution-input` |
10→| `register` | `register.py` | orch → Task: a worker's stage-report into `log` + `finish` or `unit … return` |
| `register-review` | `register_review.py` | orch → Task: review-findings into `add-document` + a `note` event |
| `commit` | `commit.py` | Task → orch: one scoped operation commit as a stage-result `commits[]` fragment |
| `launch` | `launch.py` | orch → Task: a role's launch command line with the model resolved from Task's provider mapping |

The bridge is also the plugin of orch's extension point `orch:work-source` (`extension.json`, entrypoint
`worksource.py`, `unit.json` `provides.ports`): see [Work source](#work-source).

Run a verb through the Task dispatcher: `plan.py bridge planner-orch <verb> [args…]`. `plan.py bridge list`
validates `bridge.json` and lists the verbs.
20→
## brief

```text
plan.py bridge planner-orch brief <plan> <item> [--unit U#] [--inline-reads] [--out FILE] [--repo NAME=PATH] [--plans-root DIR]
```

Returns the worker's `exec/v1` execution-input as JSON (`$schema`
`urn:swissknifeman:orch:exec:execution-input:v1`, `provenance.generated_by.tool` `planner-orch brief`).

30→- It holds the task, scope, acceptance checks, constraints, reads with `sha256`, decisions and upstream
  results; completeness is checked without truncation (`BRIEF_INCOMPLETE` names each omission).
- Lifecycle instructions, the report API, the full plan and owner messages are excluded; the full
  coordinator pack stays reachable through `context_refs`.
- `--unit U#` briefs one unit: its goal, files (write set), checks and instructions. A unit without
  files is read-only with no write authority.
- `--inline-reads` embeds the full text of existing text reads; binary reads get `error`.
- Cross-plan decisions resolve in the current repository or through repeatable `--repo NAME=PATH` /
  `SKM_PLAN_REPOS`; an unresolved required decision refuses with `REF_UNRESOLVED`.
- Read refs become paths. A ref with no source path refuses with `REF_UNRESOLVED`, including optional
40→  reads; a declared optional artifact may still have an absent file (`exists: false`).
- `--out FILE` writes a file outside the plan directory (`OUT_INVALID` otherwise) and prints its path;
  without it the document goes to stdout. The verb never changes plan state.
- `digest` is sha256 of canonical JSON without `digest` and without the `@` suffix of `input_id`;
  `input_id` ends with `@<first 12 digest chars>`.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 refusal (stderr `CODE: message`), 2 usage. The dispatcher passes output and exit
code through unchanged, also under `plan.py --output json`.

## register
50→
```text
plan.py bridge planner-orch register <plan> <item>[/<U#>] --report REPORT.json --status STATUS --actor P/M[/E]
        [--executed-by P/M[/E]] [--attempt-id ID] [--evidence V#=PATH …] [--owner-session SESSION]
        [--gate evidence] [--plans-root DIR] [--dry-run]
```

The orch registrar role classifies the report and hands it here; the bridge maps every field into the plan
and writes **only** through `plan.py` (`PLANNER_PLAN_PY`, a subprocess), never into plan files.
Never manufacture evidence: a check that did not run is not in `checks_run`, and the bridge invents no exit
60→or verdict.

REPORT.json is the executor's stage-report (`result_contract.report`), closed — an unknown field is refused
so nothing is lost:

```text
{summary: str, changed_paths: [str], checks_run: [{id: V#, cmd, exit: int} | {id: V#, procedure, verdict: pass|fail}],
 evidence: [path], open_issues: [{text, kind: pending|deviation|blocker|difficulty|assumption|note|escalation, impact?, next?}]}
```

70→| Report field | Plan call (item) |
| --- | --- |
| `summary` + `changed_paths` | `finish … --notes "<summary>\nChanged: a, b"` |
| `checks_run` entry without evidence | `--check V#=<exit>` (`verdict` pass → 0, fail → 1) |
| `--evidence V#=PATH` argument | `--evidence V#=PATH`; the evidence file carries the exit, so no `--check` for that check |
| `evidence` path without a `--evidence` argument | named in `--notes` (`Evidence: …`) |
| issue `pending` | `--pending <text>` |
| issue `deviation` | `log <plan> <item> --type deviation --summary <text> [--impact] [--next]` and `--deviation <text>` (needs `--status done_with_deviations`) |
| issue `blocker`, `difficulty`, `assumption`, `note` | friction: `log <plan> <item> --type <kind> --summary <text> [--impact] [--next]` |
| issue `escalation` | `--escalation <text>` (needs `--status blocked`; several are joined with `; `) |
80→| worker, registrar, delivery | `--executed-by`, `--actor`, `--attempt-id` on `finish`; `--actor` on each `log` |

A unit (`<item>/<U#>`) ends with `unit <plan> <item> <U#> return --notes <summary> --changed <path>…
[--executed-by] [--attempt-id]`. Checks and evidence are named in its notes: the integrator records them with
`unit … accept|rework|reject` (`accept --evidence V#=PATH`), and the bridge prints that hint. Issues become
`log` events (`pending` as a `note` prefixed `pending: `); an escalation and any `--status` other than `done`
are refused for a unit.

Order: every `log`, then one `finish` or `return`. Idempotency: a repeat with the same `--attempt-id` is a
no-op in the core for `finish` and `return`; `log` is not deduplicated by the core, so a report with
90→`open_issues` needs `--attempt-id`, and before writing the bridge reads `plan.py --output json events <plan>
--item <item> --type <types>` and skips a `log` whose `type` and `summary` the item already has.

`--dry-run` prints the JSON list of `plan.py` argv and writes nothing. Otherwise stdout is the
registration-receipt `{"plan", "ref", "calls": [{"argv", "exit", "result": "recorded|no-op|refused",
"error"?}], "next"}`, where `next` is the `plan.py next <plan>` line. The first refused call stops the
registration (exit 1, receipt without `next`); a repeat with the same attempt id completes it.

Guards, both checked before the first call that changes the plan (the work-source port always passes both; without
them the registration behaves as described above):
100→
- `--owner-session SESSION` (fencing): `plan.py --output json get <plan> <item>` must show
  `result.executor.session` = SESSION, or `result.attempt_id` = `--attempt-id` (the item was already closed by this
  attempt, so its repeat reaches `finish` and is a no-op there); otherwise `REGISTER_STALE_OWNER`, for example after
  `start --take-over` by another session.
- `--gate evidence`: `done` and `done_with_deviations` need `--evidence` for every acceptance check of the item
  (`REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING`, also for a file that is not readable check-evidence of that check) with exit 0 (a
  procedure: verdict `pass`; `REGISTER_EVIDENCE_RED` otherwise). Paths resolve as the planner resolves them
  (repository-relative or `@plan/`). `checks_run` entries without a file never become `--check`. `blocked` passes
  without evidence; a unit return has no gate (verdict `none`).
110→
With a guard the receipt carries `"gate": {"verdict": "pass|missing|red|stale|none", "checks": {"V<n>": exit|null}}`;
a guard refusal prints the receipt with `calls: []` and that gate on stdout and `CODE: message` on stderr (exit 1).

## register-review

```text
plan.py bridge planner-orch register-review <plan> <item|phase> --findings FINDINGS.json --actor P/M[/E] [--plans-root DIR] [--dry-run]
```

120→FINDINGS.json: `{verdict: GREEN|ATTENTION|RED, reviewer: {route, session}, findings: [{severity, confidence,
location, failure_scenario, basis}], date: YYYY-MM-DD}`. The bridge records

1. `add-document <plan> --json <doc>`: knowledge `review-<ref with . and / as ->-<date>`, title
   `Review <ref> <date>`, `applies_to: [<ref>]`, sections `verdict` and `findings` (the findings as JSON). The
   document travels as `--json` text, so no temporary file appears next to the plan;
2. `log <plan> <ref> --type note --summary "review <verdict>: @plan/knowledge/<id>.json; reviewer <route>
   session <session>"` — the actual reviewer route and session, not the requested one.

A repeat is a no-op: an identical stored document and a note already in the journal are skipped.
130→
## commit

`plan.py bridge planner-orch commit <plan> <item>[/<U#>] --role executor|reviewer|fix [options of plan.py commit]`

Runs `plan.py commit <plan> <ref> … --json` as a subprocess (the bridge calls Task through its CLI, as
`register` does; nothing is imported) and prints the fragment for a stage-result:

```json
{"commits": [{"sha": "…", "role": "executor", "ref": "P1.1", "paths_digest": "<sha256>"}]}
140→```

`paths_digest` is the Task result's digest of the sorted repo-relative paths; orch computes the same value
independently (`\n`-joined, no trailing newline). Every argument after `<plan> <ref>` is passed to `plan.py
commit` unchanged. A refusal of Task (`OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `NOTHING_TO_COMMIT`, …) is printed as `CODE: message`
on stderr, exit 1. A `--dry-run` creates no commit, so the bridge refuses with `COMMIT_RESULT_INVALID`.

## Refusals of register and register-review

Bridge codes (stderr `CODE: message`, exit 1, nothing written): `REGISTER_REPORT_INVALID`,
150→`REGISTER_UNCLASSIFIED` (an `open_issues` entry without a known `kind` — classify, never guess),
`REGISTER_STATUS_MISMATCH`, `REGISTER_ATTEMPT_REQUIRED`, `REGISTER_FINDINGS_INVALID`, and the guard codes
`REGISTER_STALE_OWNER`, `REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING`, `REGISTER_EVIDENCE_RED`, `REGISTER_ITEM_UNREADABLE` (the item
cannot be read for a guard). They are bridge codes,
not core `ERROR_CODES`. A refusal of a `plan.py` call (`CODE: message` of the core) lands in the receipt as
`refused` with its `error`.

## Work source

`extension.json` (extension/v1, kind `command`, point `orch:work-source`, protocol 1) registers the bridge as the
160→work source of orch. The machine enables it in its configuration:

```toml
[aicore.plugins.planner-orch]
manifest = "<hub>/bridges/planner-orch/extension.json"
trusted = true   # passes PLANNER_ROOT, PLANNER_PLAN_PY, SKM_ORCH_ROOT, AICORE_ROOT, SKM_AICORE_EVENTS__DELIVERY
```

Untrusted, the plugin finds the planner and orch through `planner` and `orch` on `PATH`. `worksource.py` answers
`op: describe` and `op: invoke` with one plugin-response; the input and output of every op follow orch's
170→`schemas/work-source/v1`, and the plan is written only through `plan.py`.

| Op | What the bridge does |
| --- | --- |
| `claim` | Candidate: the first of `items`, else an item this run already holds (`running` of `plan.py next <plan> --parallel 1 --json`), else the first item of the first `run-items` lane; none → `status: none`. Then `get` (title, route), `context --stdout` (`orchestration.scenario`, `scenario_source`), `orch.py policy show <scenario>`, and `start <plan> <ref> --actor <P/M/E> --session <run_id> --no-scout --json`. Answer `attempt_id` = `att-<run_id>-<ref>`, `session` = `run_id`; a repeat of the same run gives the same answer, also after the item was closed by that attempt (`result.attempt_id`; no `start` then). |
| `brief` | `brief.build` in process (no plan write) → `aicore.state.blobs.put_json(..., project=<repository of the plan>)`; `plan.py add-artifact <plan> <item> --path <blob path> --role input` (a repeat is a no-op). A repeat whose brief differs only in `digest`, the `@` suffix and `provenance.source_digest` from the newest brief already declared on the item reuses that brief (declaring the brief changes the item and so the source digest). `artifact_id` = `brief-<ref with . and / as ->-<digest[:12]>`, returned to orch only (a planner artifact id names an output). |
| `register` | `register.py <plan> <ref> --report <tmp> --status S --actor <registrar> --executed-by <worker> --attempt-id <attempt_id> --evidence V#=PATH… --owner-session <run_id> --gate evidence`; `outcome` `recorded`, `no-op` (every call was a no-op) or `refused` with the code of the guard or of the refused `plan.py` call; `gate` and `receipt` from the receipt. |

| Answer | `reason_code` |
| --- | --- |
180→| claim `blocked` | `SCENARIO_UNKNOWN` (no run-policy pack for the scenario), `ITEM_OWNED` (held by another session; never taken over), or the planner's refusal of `get`, `context` or `start` |
| register `refused` | `REGISTER_STALE_OWNER`, `REGISTER_EVIDENCE_MISSING`, `REGISTER_EVIDENCE_RED`, the other register codes above, or a refusal of `log`/`finish` (`CHECKS_RED`, `EVIDENCE_INVALID`, …) |
| protocol error | `INPUT_INVALID` (not the point or an unknown op), a brief refusal of the planner (`PHASE_NOT_DETAILED`, `READ_MISSING`, …), `BRIDGE_PARTNER_UNAVAILABLE`, `AICORE_NOT_FOUND` |

## Finding orch

`brief` needs no orch: the bridge knows the format. orch is needed only for the conformance tests.
`partners.find_orch_root()` looks for a directory with `scripts/orch.py`:

1. `SKM_ORCH_ROOT`;
190→2. an `orch` command on `PATH` (its real path, two levels up).

There is no search by neighbouring folders. The planner is found the same way (`PLANNER_PLAN_PY`, `PLANNER_ROOT`,
a `planner` command on `PATH`; the dispatcher sets the first two) and the foundation by `AICORE_ROOT`, then
`_vendor/aicore`, then `packages/aicore` of the hub that holds the bridge. The bridge never imports orch; it calls `python3 <orch>/scripts/orch.py validate <kind> <file>`. When orch
is required and missing, `require_orch()` prints `BRIDGE_PARTNER_UNAVAILABLE: orch not found (set
SKM_ORCH_ROOT)` and exits 3. Check-evidence: the Task core checks its own field contract
(`plan.py schema check-evidence`) with any `$schema`, so exec/v1 check-evidence passes unconverted;
`test_conformance.py` proves it on orch's fixtures.

200→## Tests

```bash
bash bridges/planner-orch/scripts/test.sh    # with PLANNER_ROOT (and SKM_ORCH_ROOT) set
bash scripts/test-bridges.sh                 # every bridge of the hub, partners wired from the hub layout
```

`test_brief.py`, `test_register.py` and `test_commit_bridge.py` (the stage-result check skips without orch) work without orch.
`test_worksource.py` (claim, brief, register with the guards, every request and answer valid by orch's
`work-source/v1`, and describe and invoke through `aicore.ext.plugins`) runs on temporary plans and skips without orch. `test_conformance.py` (documents valid for
210→`orch.py validate`, lifecycle phrases of the bridge ⊇ orch's, orch check-evidence accepted by Task) and
`test_schema_profile.py` (orch's closed schema profile ⊇ Task's) skip when orch is not found.
`test_record_parity.py` pins every recording obligation W1–W12 to its owner; rows owned by orch roles or by
this repository's plan skip when those are absent. The hub runner `scripts/test-bridges.sh` runs these tests.

## launch

```text
plan.py bridge planner-orch launch <role> <provider> [--model M] [--effort E] [--cwd DIR] [--routing FILE]
```
220→
Prints `{argv, transport, timeout_s, model, model_class}` and starts nothing. The entry comes from the partner's
launch catalog (`orch.py launch show|argv`); the catalog holds a `model_class`, never a model. The bridge maps the
class to a model through `mappings.<provider>.class_selectors` in `configs/command-routing.json` (`--routing`
overrides the file) and the effort through `effort_selectors`. `--model` pins the exact model of an owner
selector (`reviewer grok/grok-4.7`) instead of the class mapping. Providers whose CLI takes no model
(`model_set: unknown`, grok `executor`) get no model argument; `--model` there is `LAUNCH_INVALID`. Refusals: `LAUNCH_UNKNOWN` (no entry),
`LAUNCH_INVALID` (bad request or catalog), `LAUNCH_MODEL_UNRESOLVED` (mapping has no model for the class),
`ROUTING_UNREADABLE`.

230→A reviewer on another provider (`reviewer-selection`): `plan.py bridge planner-orch launch reviewer grok --model grok-4.7
--effort high --cwd <repository>`. The grok entry runs headless under orch `scripts/ro-run.py` (Linux Landlock, no
root, no user namespaces): the filesystem stays readable, writes go only to temp directories, `~/.grok` and
`<repository>/vendor` (test caches); the brief goes on stdin (`--prompt-file /dev/stdin`), the stream is
`streaming-messages-json` under `bypassPermissions` with the edit tools disallowed. The tests also compare the argv of `scout` with Task's own `orchestration.scout`, which
`start --scout` keeps using unchanged.

are errors that name the layer, file, line and key.

example `SKM_ANALYST_RECOMPUTE__CANDIDATE_MIN_N=30`. The text is parsed by the type of the key (booleans:
`true|false|1|0|yes|no`; arrays: a JSON array). An unknown path under a known module warns once; `SKM_<MODULE>_ROOT`
locates the module's folder and is not configuration (unless the schema has a top-level key `root`).

Checking the config-inventory diff for added content. Verifying whether validate_node's oneOf logic correctly handles problems().

Investigating a potential evidence gate bug where acceptance checks may write partial evidence despite the planner requiring a subject. Also examining `op_register` for exit code handling.

Argparse errors exit with code 2, which correctly raises a plugin error. Outcome detection for no-op registration messages was verified against the expected string patterns.

Found a potential crash in `register.py`. Journal reads use `--output json`, but the code expects the top-level JSON to be a list of events. If the API returns an object containing an `events` array instead, `json.loads(done.stdout)["data"]` will raise a TypeError. That uncaught exception would crash the script and cause it to exit with code 1, which the worksource treats as a refusal.

The TypeError crash would occur before any writes, so the worksource receives no receipt and treats the failure as a refusal. Existing tests only verify an empty events list, which does not cover a misshapen JSON structure.

The journal JSON structure is confirmed to be a list, so the earlier TypeError crash hypothesis does not apply.

The `_source_register` CLI writes the receipt into the run directory rather than the plan file. This is acceptable.

In `prepare`, the scenario is loaded from the claim document with a fallback to the default profile. A null or empty scenario string stored in `run.json` would be treated as falsy and fall back to the default profile.

If the orchestration scenario is null, `policy_exists` is skipped and the plugin raises `Blocked SCENARIO_UNKNOWN`, preventing an invalid start.

A partial route object may fail client validation after start. The default route contains both `class` and `effort`. If a plugin item supplies a route with extra fields, the plugin strips them down to those two required keys.

A route with only `class` and no `effort` fails schema validation after the item starts. The client then returns `WORK_SOURCE_FAILED`. Retrying resumes the same session, but the invalid route persists, so the item remains stuck in `in_progress` owned by the run while the orchestrator has no `run.json`. I am checking whether the planner route schema actually permits a class-only route.

The planner and orchestrator scenario output patterns match exactly, so no bug exists there. Item references do not contain slashes, which is safe. I am now examining `problems()` for a validation hole.

The schema $id and registry base URN resolve correctly for the claim definition. Nested $refs such as actor should be validated if the walker follows them. External artifact-ref references may fail resolution if the registry lacks those schemas, but passing tests suggest they are present.

I will run the tests to see whether the external artifact-ref schema resolves correctly or if validation errors would reject valid briefs.

The `op_brief` add-artifact logic is sound. `blob_path` accepts an artifact-ref dictionary, and the resulting path resolves under the project directory so `relative_to` produces a valid relative path for the `add-artifact` command.

The `.swissknifeman` directory is not a plan file, so it is correctly excluded from plan processing. In `_previous_brief`, the blob path resolves to an `artifacts/sha256/<hex>` directory, and using `path.name` as the tagged digest is valid.

I need to understand source_digest.

The source_digest is computed from the full item including artifacts, so it changes whenever artifacts are added. The worker view strips this field. Other brief fields derive from the item title, summary, scope, and checks rather than the artifact list directly. I am checking whether _context_refs or other brief fields also change when artifacts are added.

{"type":"ReadFile","FileContent":{"content":"1→# exec/v1 contracts

Engine-neutral documents exchanged between plan bridges, roles and engine bindings. The schemas in
`schemas/exec/v1/` are the source of truth; this page is a short map.
Engine operations and run states are described in [engine-port.md](engine-port.md).

## Conventions

- JSON Schema draft 2020-12 in the closed keyword profile of the aicore validator (`orch.schema` re-exports `aicore.util.schema`; orch keeps no profile of its own).
10→  Numeric bounds and cross-field rules are semantic checks in `orch.contracts.semantic_checks`.
- Every document carries `$schema` (`urn:swissknifeman:orch:exec:<kind>:v1`) and
  `contract_version: "exec/v1"`. An unknown version is refused with `CONTRACT_VERSION`.
- Objects are closed (`additionalProperties: false`) except `extensions`, run-event `data`,
  effect-receipt `expected_prior`/`result`/`precondition.observed_prior`, launch-plan `env` and `config.values`
  (the open map of configuration values; its digest, not its schema, pins the content).
- `canonical_digest(doc)` is sha256 of sorted compact JSON without `digest`, with the `@digest`
  suffix removed from `input_id`; it is computed with the canonical JSON of aicore (`digest/v1`), and the
  `exec/v1` form stays the bare lowercase hex without the `sha256:` tag. A document with a float or a lone surrogate is not canonical JSON:
  `validate` reports `DIGEST_MISMATCH` next to the schema issue.
20→- Shared definitions (`id`, `sha256`, `ts`, `path`, `provider`, `modelClass`, `effort`, `route`,
  `check`, `support`, `binding`, `roleId`, `commitRole`, `submissionId`, `attemptId`, `callId`, `eventId`,
  `moduleVersion`, `reasonCode`, `skillRef`) live in [`defs.schema.json`](../schemas/exec/v1/defs.schema.json).

Validate a document: `python3 packages/orch/scripts/orch.py validate <kind> <file.json>`.
Diagnostics include `path`, `code`, `message` and `level`. Warning-only documents return exit 0;
errors return exit 1. `--quiet` suppresses stdout while preserving diagnostics and the exit status.

## Documents

30→| Kind | Written by | Read by | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`execution-input`](../schemas/exec/v1/execution-input.schema.json) | plan bridge `brief`, ad-hoc/review input | engine, prompt render, role | What to do: goal, scope, acceptance, minimum route, result contract |
| [`run-policy`](../schemas/exec/v1/run-policy.schema.json) | owner/config, outside plan JSON | engine | Stage pipeline, review limits, retries, git and finalize actions |
| [`role-manifest`](../schemas/exec/v1/role-manifest.schema.json) | orch `roles/` | binding, skill resolver | Instruction references, skills, tool permissions, write authority |
| [`capability-record`](../schemas/exec/v1/capability-record.schema.json) | binding seeds, probes | `prepare` | What one binding × provider × CLI version supports |
| [`launch-plan`](../schemas/exec/v1/launch-plan.schema.json) | `EnginePort.prepare` | `run`, reviewer | Resolved stages with argv/profile/prompt and refusals |
| [`run-event`](../schemas/exec/v1/run-event.schema.json) | binding `watch` | `RunState` | Normalized event of a running stage |
| [`stage-result`](../schemas/exec/v1/stage-result.schema.json) | `RunState.stage_result`, binding | coordinator, registrar | Outcome of one stage attempt |
| [`effect-receipt`](../schemas/exec/v1/effect-receipt.schema.json) | engine | engine, reconcile | Idempotent record of an external effect |
40→| [`check-evidence`](../schemas/exec/v1/check-evidence.schema.json) | engine, executor, human | plan store `finish`, reviewer | Proof that an acceptance check ran on a candidate tree |

### execution-input

| Field | Req. | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input_id`, `digest` | * | `<ref>@<digest[:12]>`; canonical digest of the document |
| `provenance` | * | one of `plan` (plan, item, unit, source digest, generator), `adhoc`, `review` |
| `goal`, `scope` | * | expected result; `include`, `exclude`, `write_set`, `read_only` |
| `acceptance` | * | `checks` (each has exactly one of `cmd`/`procedure`), `deliverables` |
50→| `route` | * | `minimum` route: class and effort, never bypassed |
| `result_contract` | * | report fields, `write_authority`, `commit_owner: coordinator`, `plan_mutation: forbidden` |
| `why`, `guidance`, `sections`, `constraints`, `decisions`, `reads`, `context_refs`, `upstream`, `lessons`, `hints`, `escalation` | | full item context, never truncated |
| `provenance.commit` | | commit that the references of a `plan` input are pinned to |

Semantic: digest and `input_id` suffix match; no lifecycle phrases (`LIFECYCLE_LEAK`) outside the

| `isolation` | | `mode: worktree\|shared`, `integration: sequential`, `recheck: item\|all\|none`; all three fields required when present |
| `version` | | policy version (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) |
| `sandbox` | | permissions of the stages (`permissions/v1` of aicore: `filesystem`, `network`, `shell`, `env`, `profile`, …) |
| `on_error` | | action by failure class: the 12 classes of `error/v1` and `unknown_outcome`, each `{action, max?}` with `action` one of `stop`, `retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`, `replan`, `reconcile` |
| `fallback_routes` | | `{provider, model_class}` routes that `fallback_route` may switch to, in order |
| `budgets` | | `brief_max_bytes`, `packer_input_max_bytes`, `stage_tokens_max` (integers ≥ 0) |
| `stages[].limits` | | `input_tokens_max`, `output_tokens_max` of the stage; `stages[].kind` also accepts `condense` (a model stage that condenses the optional part of a brief) |

Engine-neutral documents exchanged between plan bridges, roles and engine bindings. The schemas in

## Conventions

- JSON Schema draft 2020-12 in the closed keyword profile of the aicore validator (`orch.schema` re-exports `aicore.util.schema`; orch keeps no profile of its own).
  Numeric bounds and cross-field rules are semantic checks in `orch.contracts.semantic_checks`.
- Every document carries `$schema` (`urn:swissknifeman:orch:exec:<kind>:v1`) and
  `contract_version: "exec/v1"`. An unknown version is refused with `CONTRACT_VERSION`.
- Objects are closed (`additionalProperties: false`) except `extensions`, run-event `data`,
  effect-receipt `expected_prior`/`result`/`precondition.observed_prior`, launch-plan `env` and `config.values`
  (the open map of configuration values; its digest, not its schema, pins the content).
- `canonical_digest(doc)` is sha256 of sorted compact JSON without `digest`, with the `@digest`
  suffix removed from `input_id`; it is computed with the canonical JSON of aicore (`digest/v1`), and the
  `exec/v1` form stays the bare lowercase hex without the `sha256:` tag. A document with a float or a lone surrogate is not canonical JSON:
  `validate` reports `DIGEST_MISMATCH` next to the schema issue.
